from kinloom import Kinloom
from kinloom.talk import Talk

kl = Kinloom()

# --- stand-ins for the game -------------------------------------------------
player_name = "Ana"
gold = 12
guard = {"name": "GUARD", "post": "the north gate"}

def give_item(item):
    print(f"the guard hands over {item}")

def record_heard(wav_bytes):
    return wav_bytes  # the game already has the microphone buffer

# --- the guard, declared once ----------------------------------------------
kl.character(
    "GUARD",
    soul="a bored gate guard at the north gate, dry and literal, loyal to the watch, who lets friends through and "
         "remembers who was rude to him",
    tools={"give_item": {"item": "text"}, "open_gate": {}},
)

# --- talking instead of typing ---------------------------------------------
talk = Talk(kl, "GUARD", speaker=player_name, facts=lambda: {"gold": gold, "post": guard["post"]},
            on_action=lambda tool, args: give_item(args["item"]))

# what the game does when the player holds the talk key and speaks
held_wav = record_heard(b"RIFF....WAVE")          # the microphone buffer the game captured
heard = kl.listen(held_wav)                       # "" if nothing was said
if heard:
    reply = talk.send(heard)                      # the guard answers what the player said
    audio = kl.speak("GUARD", reply)
    if audio:
        play(audio.data)                          # or show reply as text when there is no voice

# while the talk key is held, the guard keeps deciding with the game's functions
for tool, args in kl.act("GUARD", {"gold": gold}, think=False):
    if tool == "open_gate":
        print("the gate creaks open")

# each frame, where the game would
talk.update()

kl.character("MARCHAND", "a gruff old market merchant who haggles and knows every price in town",
             voice="low, warm")

# the game hands us a recording (here: a stand-in for bytes from the microphone)
def record_from_microphone():
    return b"RIFF....WAVE"          # real game: the WAV bytes captured while the player held the key

# the game plays a WAV (here: just note it)
def play(audio):
    print("playing:", audio.path)

# --- where the game would do it --------------------------------------------
said = kl.listen(record_from_microphone())          # what the player said ("" if nothing)

    reply = kl.chat("MARCHAND", said, {"gold": 12, "goods": "apples"}, speaker="PLAYER")
